I read all 57 lines of the file. It introduces no definitions, structures, classes, instances, notations or abbreviations. It only contains three results:
- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomBranch_point`: computes the bottom Hecke branch point.
- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_periodization`: rewrites the bottom branch sum as a horizontal periodization.
- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_mean`: the integral identity built on the first two.

Every concept these results use is defined in other files: `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBranchPoint`, `cubicThetaHorizontalPoint`, `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization`, `cubicThetaSectionHorizontal`, `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum`, `Eisenstein` and `primaryPrime`. The rubric asks whether a file creates its own competing version of a concept, and it explicitly excludes standalone theorem duplication and proof shortening. This file declares no concept at all, so the rubric has nothing to apply to here. Whether the definitions it uses duplicate Mathlib concepts should be judged when reviewing the files that define them.
